L583@P11: A mixed integer linear program was formulated in the
L584@P11: GAMS environment (GAMS Development Corporation,
L585@P11: Washington, DC) and the optimum solution was found
L586@P11: using the ILOG CPLEX 8.100 solver (ILOG, Inc. Mountain
L587@P11: View, CA).
L588@P11: Optimization
L589@P11: Unlike heterotrophic organisms that utilize the same substrate as the source of both carbon and energy, photoautotrophic organisms require two substrates, one for energy
L590@P11: (light) and one for carbon (carbon dioxide). Due to the
L591@P11: input of two substrates, FBA simulations can be run in
L592@P11: either light or carbon limitation conditions. To simulate
L593@P11: carbon limitation, the model is allowed unlimited light,
L594@P11: which calculates an optimal biomass flux. No fermentation products were detected in the media during growth
L595@P11: (see maximum uptake rates discussion) therefore, in the
L596@P11: absence of carbon overflow products, the yield of biomass
L597@P11: is fixed because the only outlet for carbon is biomass. For
L598@P11: photoautotrophic metabolism, a more meaningful result
L599@P11: is to find the flux distribution that maximizes biomass
L600@P11: while minimizing energy usage. Therefore the optimization is done in two steps. The first step is to maximize biomass with no constraint on light and the second is to fix
L601@P11: the biomass and minimize light. Flux distributions for the
L602@P11: heterotrophic case are the result of a one-step optimization to maximize biomass.
L603@P11: Culture conditions
L604@P11: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii strain CC-400 cw15 mt+ was
L605@P11: acquired from the Chlamydomonas Genetics Center. Cells
L606@P11: were cultivated at 25°C in 250 ml flasks with a working
L607@P11: volume of 50 ml and an agitation rate of 200 RPM. Heterotrophic and mixotrophic cells were grown in TAP media
L608@P11: [43] and autotrophic cells were grown in similar media
L609@P11: without addition of acetic acid. Mixotrophic and
L610@P11: autotrophic cultures were grown under constant illumination at an average fluence rate of 65 μE/m2/s. All cells were
L611@P11: grown in the presence of atmospheric carbon dioxide levels. Growth was monitored spectrophotometrically by
L612@P11: measuring absorbance at 750 nm.
L613@P11: Maximum uptake rates
L614@P11: In order to add constraints on nutrient and light uptake to
L615@P11: the model, additional experimental measurements were
L616@P11: taken. Maximum growth rates were measured for all three
L617@P11: growth conditions from three separate experiments. The
L618@P11: results are shown in Table 7. For autotrophic growth, the
L619@P11: maximum carbon dioxide uptake rate was calculated to be
L620@P11: 2.04 mmol/g biomass/hr. The maximum solar light flux
L621@P11: was set to be 2100 μE/m2/s [44]. For heterotrophic
L622@P11: growth, the maximum acetate uptake rate was measured
L623@P11: using high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)
L624@P11: coupled to an refractive index detector (RID) detector and
L625@P11: was found to be 12.06 mmol/g biomass/hr. The same
L626@P11: HPLC method was used to look for fermentation products, but none were detected and therefore they were not
L627@P11: included in the model. The biomass growth yield on acetate was measured in exponentially growing cells to be
L628@P11: 3.12 ± 0.23 kg biomass/100 moles acetate from three
L629@P11: independent experiments.
L630@P11: Estimation of cell surface area
L631@P11: In order to convert the calculated total photons from the
L632@P11: model to a flux (μE/m2/s), the surface area per kilogram
L633@P11: biomass must be calculated. Based on experimental measurements, the dry weight of a typical C. reinhardtii was
L634@P11: determined to be 0.2 pg. The length and width of cell were
L635@P11: assumed to be 10 μm and 3 μm respectively [43] based on
L636@P11: literature values. The geometry of the cell was assumed to
L637@P11: be a prolate spheroid. The surface area per kilogram biomass was then calculated to be 389 m2kg-1.
L638@P11: Maintenance requirements
L639@P11: Growth associated and non-growth associated maintenance requirements were also included in the model.

L680@P12: Growth associated energy is included to account for partially unknown energy requirements for transport, biosynthesis and polymerization [42] while non-growth
L681@P12: associated accounts for cellular maintenance operations
L682@P12: such as DNA repair, cell wall maintenance, and pH control. Growth associated maintenance was found to be
L683@P12: 29.89 mmol ATP/g biomass by fitting the model to the
L684@P12: experimentally determined biomass yield by changing the
L685@P12: ATP requirement. This value falls into the range of published values for growth associated maintenance values
L686@P12: [2-7]. Autotrophic and mixotrophic maintenance requirements were assumed to be the same. Non-growth associated maintenance requirements range from 0.36 mmol
L687@P12: ATP/g DW hr for Lactobacillus plantarum to 7.60 mmol
L688@P12: ATP/g DW for E. coli. For C. reinhardtii, non-growth associated maintenance was assumed to be 1.50 mmol ATP/g
L689@P12: DW [3,5,7].
L690@P12: Biomass composition
L691@P12: The biomass composition was determined separately for
L692@P12: each of the three growth regimes: autotrophic, mixotrophic and heterotrophic growth. Lipids were measured
L693@P12: using the chloroform-methanol extraction method of Ishida et al. [45]. The resulting water layer and pellet were
L694@P12: then dried and resuspended in 0.2 N NaOH and diluted
L695@P12: by a factor of 5. This solution was then assayed for protein
L696@P12: content with the Pierce BCA protein assay kit (Pierce Biotechnology, Inc. Rockford, IL). The amino acid composition (Additional file 3) was estimated from Gas
L697@P12: chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis of
L698@P12: hydrolyzed protein (data not shown). Chlorophyll a and
L699@P12: b were measured [43] and subtracted from the total lipid
L700@P12: measurement. DNA and RNA were assumed to be constant for all growth conditions; the DNA content was
L701@P12: determined by Chiang et al[46] to be 1.23 × 10-7 μg per
L702@P12: cell and the RNA content was assumed to be 28-fold
L703@P12: higher than the DNA content [47]. The GC content of
L704@P12: DNA was measured to be 62.1% [43] and the same GC
L705@P12: content was assumed for RNA. Carbohydrate composition was calculated as the balance of the fraction dry
L706@P12: weight. The elemental composition of lyophilized cells
L707@P12: was also determined. In all cases except elemental composition, experiments were done in triplicate.
